key_insight: Instance-specific, checklist-style rubrics can turn coarse preference signals into fine-grained rewards, enabling Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to better capture subtle visual reasoning differences. rDPO uses these rubric rewards to align multimodal model outputs with what actually matters per image-instruction pair.
problem_solved: Existing preference-data pipelines rely on off-policy perturbations or coarse outcome signals that fail to capture fine-grained visual criteria, hurting preference optimization for multimodal tasks.
method: Generate an instance-specific rubric (checklist of essential and additional criteria) for each image-instruction pair to define what 'good' means locally.
Translate rubric assessments into reward/preference signals that reflect fine-grained visual reasoning rather than coarse outcomes.
Apply Direct Preference Optimization using these rubric-derived rewards (rDPO) to train multimodal models with more meaningful preference supervision.
impact: rDPO provides practitioners a practical way to produce higher-quality preference data for vision-language tasks, improving alignment and evaluation on subtle visual reasoning aspects without relying on brittle perturbation schemes.
